verified_facts: The Land Theme contains point, line and polygon land-cover features
Land cover and Land Use describe different concepts
the theme contains Land, Land Point, Landform, Landform Line and Landform Point
coverage is Great Britain and the default CRS is EPSG:27700
updates can be up to daily
supply formats and access mechanisms differ by feature type
Land is a polygon for surface areas not otherwise captured as specified building, transport, structure or water feature types
schema 3.2 made containing-site and lower-tier-authority counts nullable
habitat percentages are rounded to the nearest five percent with a minimum of ten percent
Land Point represents a small land feature not captured as specified polygon or other point feature types
the same OSID may occur in more than one feature type
Landform Point is a point representation of a distinct physical morphology too small for polygon capture
capture specification context does not make the point a height observation
the Transport Theme has RAMI, Transport Features and Transport Network collections
OSID, TOID, USRN and collection-specific identifiers have distinct roles
the collection is a topologically structured link-and-node representation of GB road, ferry, rail and path networks
path surface and cross-network connectivity are explicit network attributes
Path is a link set of Path Links sharing a name
a Path Link may be referenced by multiple Path features
the Path-to-Path-Link cross-reference carries path and link identifiers plus path version date
Path Link is a linear connectivity object between start and end Path Nodes
capture includes otherwise uninferred links and excludes specified non-public or obstructed paths
surface, names, match status, grade separation, lighting and cycle attribution have separate meanings
Path Node is a point used to split the path network for connectivity
schema 1.1 launched 28 July 2025
temporal requests before a schema launch can be inconsistent
the product is a topologically connected road, track, path and rights-of-way network for GB National Parks
its source portfolio includes topography, highways and terrain products
the Named Features collection contains Crowd Sourced Name Point, Named Area, Named Point and Named Road Junction
the same named feature representations share an OSID
the collection supplies names of features and places of geographic significance
crowd-sourced and authoritative name representations require feature-type provenance
OS NGD is organised into themes, collections, feature types and features
feature type is the most granular schema grouping
published 13 May 2026 and represents a January 2026 snapshot
fixed availability, take-up and mobile prediction measures are distinct
decent broadband is at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload
fixed and mobile downloads are separate
maximum available speed and active-connection performance are separate products
no fixed-performance postcode file is produced from 2024 onward
ONSPD and NSPL use different allocation methodologies
ONSPD includes current and terminated UK postcodes
products are released quarterly in February, May, August and November
NSUL assigns current GB addresses to Output Areas by UPRN point-in-polygon and higher geographies by best fit
ONSUD allocates addresses directly to geographies using UPRN grid references
